turns.prompt_text: I got a bamboo lab A1 and I need to replace the AMS tubes
turns.response_html:
The Bambu Lab A1 requires specific PTFE tubing with an inner diameter (ID) of 2.5mm and an outer diameter (OD) of 4mm. Using standard 2mm ID tubing can cause excessive friction and loading errors in the AMS lite system.

Replacement Guide

To replace the tubes, ensure the printer is powered off and all filament is unloaded.

  • Removal from Filament Hub: Use tweezers to press down the black pneumatic connector on top of the hub. While holding the connector down, gently push the tube toward the hub and then pull it straight out.
  • Removal from AMS lite: Press the ring-shaped connector on the feeder unit with your fingers to release the locking mechanism and pull the tube out.
  • A1 Tube Lengths: The A1 uses longer tubes than the A1 Mini to accommodate its larger build volume. The standard lengths are 730mm (x2) and 830mm (x2).

Recommended Replacement Tubes

You can purchase pre-cut sets or bulk rolls. If buying bulk, ensure you use a dedicated PTFE cutter to get a perfectly square 90-degree cut, which prevents filament jams.

Bambu Lab PTFE Tube
This is the genuine replacement tubing specifically designed for the lower friction requirements of the Bambu Lab ecosystem. It maintains the critical 2.5mm internal clearance for reliable high-speed retractions.

  • Specifications: 2.5mm ID / 4mm OD
  • Material: High-grade PTFE
  • Best For: Maintaining factory performance and reliability.

PTFE Tube Kit with Cutter
For a more cost-effective long-term solution, a bulk 5-meter roll allows you to cut custom lengths for both the AMS lite and the internal toolhead paths. This kit includes a sharp tubing cutter, which is essential for making the clean, flat cuts required for the pneumatic joints to seal properly.

  • Kit Includes: 5m of 2.5mm x 4mm tubing and 1 industrial cutter.
  • Advantage: Allows for multiple replacements and custom routing setups.

Summary for Choosing

  • Choose the Genuine Bambu Lab Tube if you want a guaranteed "drop-in" fit with the exact friction coefficients tested by the manufacturer.
  • Choose the PTFE Tube Kit if you prefer to have extra material on hand for future maintenance and need the specialized cutter to ensure your manual cuts don't cause feeding issues.

If you would like, I can find a set of printable tube organizers or "cable chains" to help manage the new tubes and prevent them from tangling during high-speed moves. Would you like me to look for those?

turns.prompt_text: let me rephrase that I have the tubing I've just cut them off at the point of the bamboo lab head and I need to remove the extra there and reattach the AMS system
turns.response_html:
To remove the remaining PTFE tubing from the toolhead and reattach your AMS lite system, follow these steps:

Remove Stuck Tubing

  1. Heat the nozzle to the printing temperature of the last filament used (e.g., 220°C for PLA) to soften any plastic holding the tube in place.
  2. Press down on the black pneumatic connector (the "collar") at the top of the toolhead with your fingernail or tweezers.
  3. While the collar is depressed, pull the short segment of tubing straight up and out.

Reattach the AMS System

  • Check the Cut: Ensure your new tubes have a clean, 90-degree flat cut. An angled or crushed cut will cause friction and loading errors.
  • Insert Tubing: Push the tube firmly into the toolhead connector until it seats completely. Give it a light tug to ensure the internal teeth have gripped the tube.
  • Connect to AMS lite: Insert the other end into the corresponding feeder port on the AMS lite unit until it clicks into place.

If the tube is stuck too deep to grab, I can find a guide on opening the toolhead cover to access the internal extruder assembly. Would you like those instructions?
